mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the Federal Funds rate above 4% in the month prior to the decision is associated with a negative 20-day S&P 500 forward return due to higher discount rates eroding expected equity payoffs.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above 4% in the prior month
regime_hint: tightening cycle after a period of easing
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically different from zero when FEDFUNDS > 4% in prior month (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: Rising unemployment claims (PAYEMS) accompanied by a simultaneous decline in consumer price inflation (CPIAUCSL) predicts a positive 60-day S&P 500 forward return as labor market softness offsets inflationary pressure.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases while CPIAUCSL decreases in the same month
regime_hint: labor market weakening with cooling inflation
failure_condition: Over 60-day horizon, returns are negative or statistically indistinguishable from zero (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A monthly surge in industrial production (INDPRO) exceeding 2% year-over-year followed by a subsequent drop in consumer demand proxy (HOUST) predicts a negative 20-day S&P 500 forward return as over-supply in manufacturing crowds out equity demand.
regime_hint: overheating industrial cycle followed by softening demand
failure_condition: 20-day returns are positive or not significantly different from zero (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A consecutive decline in both industrial production (INDPRO) and consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) for two consecutive months predicts a positive 5-day S&P 500 forward return as market anticipates easing supply constraints.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are not positive or are negative (p < 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate falls below 4% (UNRATE) without a corresponding rise in inflation (CPIAUCSL), the S&P 500 is expected to deliver a positive 20-day forward return as low unemployment signals economic strength.
regime_hint: labor market tightening with stable or falling inflation

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in payrolls (PAYEMS) for three consecutive months predicts a negative 60-day S&P 500 forward return as wage growth fuels inflationary expectations and compresses real equity returns.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases each month for 3 consecutive months

mechanism_narrative: A sharp drop in retail sales proxy (implied via HOUST) coinciding with a decline in consumer confidence (not available, so using HOUST as a demand proxy) predicts a negative 20-day S&P 500 forward return as weak demand weighs on equities.
candidate_trigger: HOUST falls by >10% from prior month
failure_condition: 20-day returns are positive or not significantly different from zero (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When industrial production (INDPRO) remains flat for two consecutive months while the unemployment rate (UNRATE) rises, the S&P 500 is expected to post a positive 60-day forward return as market anticipates supply-side imbalances resolving into growth.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO unchanged for two months and UNRATE increases
regime_hint: supply stagnation with rising labor market pressures
